transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Ever since that car drove into the crowd, even little sounds make me feel like I’m back there and I jump out of my chair or drop things. I just feel so on edge, and my nerves are completely shot.
How long has it been since the car drove into the crowd, and have these symptoms lasted more than a month?
It's only been about a week since that awful day at the street fair. So no, it hasn't been a month yet, but every single day since it happened has felt like a lifetime.

Since the accident, have you had moments where you felt numb, detached from yourself, or like things around you weren’t real? Have there been times you couldn’t remember important parts of what happened?

I don't really feel numb or detached, but I definitely have big blank spots in my memory of that day. I remember setting up the booth and then suddenly I was holding someone's hand on the ground, but I can't piece together how I got from one moment to the next. It's like those parts of the event are just completely blocked out.
Since the accident, have you been having unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about what happened, or do you find yourself avoiding reminders of the street fair?

Yes, it’s like a film stuck on repeat in my mind showing that car jumping the curb and my friend's body flying, and I keep waking up at night with those same images. I’ve also been avoiding reminders by turning down rides past downtown and skipping Mass and the senior center because thinking about busy streets or crowds makes my chest tighten.
Since the accident happened only a week ago, have there been any periods when these symptoms completely went away, or have they been present most of the time every day since then?

No, they haven't gone away at all; it has been a constant, non-stop struggle every single day since it happened. From the moment I wake up until I try to go to sleep, I am completely on edge. I haven't had a single day where I felt back to my normal self or got any relief.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed trauma-related symptoms within one week of directly experiencing a catastrophic event (car drove into a crowd). Symptoms include intrusive recollections, nightmares, hyperarousal/startle, avoidance of reminders, and dissociative amnesia for parts of the event. Duration is less than 1 month, which supports acute stress reaction rather than PTSD.
